title: Staffing Firm Placement Capacity Score
subtitle: Find the bottleneck between your team size and your placement volume

persona_selector.text: What size is your staffing firm right now?

answers.label: Solo or 2-9 employees, scrappy mode
10-25 employees, growing fast
26-50 employees, structured but stretched
51-75 employees, scaling and feeling the drag

questions.text: When a new job order comes in from a client, how long before a recruiter has it in hand and ready to work?

answers.label: More than 24 hours, sometimes days
Within 12-24 hours, depends on who is around
Within 4-12 hours during business days
Within 1-4 hours consistently
Under 1 hour, automated routing in place

questions.text: How is job order information captured from the client today?

answers.label: Email threads and phone notes, nothing structured
A shared doc or spreadsheet someone updates
Intake form, but data still gets re-typed into the ATS
Intake form that pushes directly into our ATS
Automated intake with validation, enrichment, and instant ATS sync

questions.text: How do you qualify a new client or job order before committing recruiter time?

answers.label: We take everything and figure it out later
Gut check from the owner or senior recruiter
Loose checklist, applied inconsistently
Standard scorecard run by one person
Automated scoring with clear go or no-go criteria

questions.text: When a job order is assigned to a recruiter, what does the handoff look like?

answers.label: A Slack message or a yell across the office
Email with attachments, recruiter rebuilds context
Ticket in a tool, but missing half the details
Structured assignment in the ATS with full client context
Automated assignment with brief, history, and starter shortlist attached

low.headline: Your intake is the leak, and it is a big one
low.text: Job orders are entering your firm through informal channels and losing hours or days before a recruiter touches them. Every hour of delay here compounds downstream because candidates get poached, clients lose patience, and your team starts every search behind the clock.
steps: Build one standard intake form that every client and rep funnels into, no exceptions
Pipe that form directly into your ATS so nothing gets re-typed
Set a hard service level of 2 hours from intake to recruiter assignment, and track it weekly

mid.headline: Intake works, but it is held together by people not systems
mid.text: You have process, but it depends on specific humans being available and paying attention. That works until volume spikes or someone takes a vacation, and then everything backs up. The fix is removing the human dependency from the routing and capture layer.
steps: Audit every job order from the last 30 days and map where time was lost between client contact and recruiter assignment
Add automated routing rules so assignments happen the moment intake is complete
Build a daily intake dashboard so bottlenecks are visible before they cost you a placement

high.headline: Intake is a real competitive advantage for you
high.text: You are fast, structured, and your recruiters get high-context handoffs. Now the use is in pushing intake from reactive to proactive, using client signals to anticipate orders before they land.
steps: Use client hiring patterns and historical data to forecast incoming orders weekly
Pre-build candidate shortlists for recurring client needs before the order lands
Layer in client-facing portals so clients self-serve order submission and status updates

questions.text: When a new job order comes in, what does your candidate pipeline look like for that role?

answers.label: We start sourcing from zero every time
We search the ATS, but most records are stale
We have a rough talent pool, but it is not tagged well
We have a tagged pool we can filter quickly
We have warm, recently-contacted candidates ready for most common roles

questions.text: How many distinct sourcing channels are actively contributing candidates each month?

answers.label: One, basically just LinkedIn or one job board
Two channels, but one does most of the work
Three to four channels, manually managed
Four to five channels with some automation
Five or more channels, fully automated and measured

questions.text: How do you re-engage candidates you have placed or interviewed before?

answers.label: We do not, they go cold
Occasional outreach when we remember
Monthly newsletter or check-in
Scheduled nurture sequences by skill or vertical
Automated re-engagement triggered by role openings

questions.text: How clean and current is the candidate data in your ATS?

answers.label: Honestly, it is a graveyard
Most records are outdated, we work around it
Recent placements are clean, the rest is mixed
We run quarterly cleanups and tagging
Automated enrichment and refresh keeps records current

low.headline: You are sourcing from scratch every single time
low.text: Your team is paying the full sourcing cost on every order, which means recruiters are spending more time hunting than placing. The fastest revenue surface here is turning your ATS from a graveyard into an active pipeline.
steps: Run a one-time ATS cleanup focused on your top 3 most common role types
Set up automated outreach sequences to re-engage past candidates monthly
Add at least one new sourcing channel and instrument it so you know what it produces

mid.headline: You have a pipeline, but it is not doing enough work for you
mid.text: You have a pool of candidates, but it is not actively warm and it is not consistently tagged. That means every order still requires a sourcing sprint instead of a quick filter and outreach. Tighten the tagging and nurture and you will cut your time-to-shortlist in half.
steps: Standardize your tagging taxonomy across skills, locations, and availability windows
Build automated nurture sequences segmented by skill vertical
Track candidate response rates by channel and double down on the top two performers

high.headline: Your pipeline is a real asset, now monetize it
high.text: You have warm, tagged, and active candidates. The next move is using that asset to win business, not just fill orders. Firms with a pipeline like yours can sell speed as a service.
steps: Pitch clients on guaranteed shortlist times backed by your pipeline depth
Build a private talent showcase you can share with key accounts
Add predictive sourcing that fills pipeline gaps before the order arrives

questions.text: From job order to first qualified shortlist of candidates sent to the client, how long does it typically take?

answers.label: More than 5 business days
3 to 5 business days
2 to 3 business days
24 to 48 hours
Under 24 hours consistently

questions.text: How is candidate qualification handled before they hit a client interview?

answers.label: Whatever the recruiter feels like asking that day
A loose script, applied inconsistently
Standard screening questions, manually run
Structured screening with scoring rubric
Automated screening that pre-qualifies before recruiter time

questions.text: How do you match candidates to job orders today?

answers.label: Recruiter memory and gut feel
Keyword search in the ATS
Tag and filter combinations
Scored matching across multiple criteria
AI-assisted matching with explainable rankings

questions.text: How are candidate submissions to clients formatted and delivered?

answers.label: Raw resume attached to an email
Resume plus a few notes in the email body
Branded summary, manually built each time
Templated submission pack auto-generated from ATS
Client portal with structured profiles and live status

low.headline: Your matching speed is costing you placements
low.text: If shortlists take more than 3 business days, you are losing candidates to faster competitors and watching clients go cold. The qualification step is almost certainly the biggest time sink, and it is the easiest one to systematize.
steps: Document your top 10 screening questions and build them into a standard scorecard
Pre-screen candidates with an automated intake before recruiter calls
Set a 48-hour shortlist target and measure every order against it

mid.headline: You match well, but you match slowly
mid.text: Your team produces quality shortlists, but the speed is not where it needs to be to win competitive searches. The lever here is removing manual steps from qualification and submission so recruiter time goes into relationship work, not formatting.
steps: Automate the candidate submission pack generation from your ATS
Add scored matching so recruiters spend less time deciding who to call first
Track time-to-shortlist weekly and treat anything over 48 hours as a process bug

high.headline: Speed is your edge, now scale it
high.text: You are fast, accurate, and your submissions look professional. The next layer is using that speed to take on more orders per recruiter without dropping quality.
steps: Add AI-assisted matching to handle the first pass on every order
Open a client-facing portal so clients can review and move candidates without back-and-forth
Benchmark your speed publicly and use it in your sales pitch

questions.text: How much of an average recruiter's day is spent on administrative work versus actual recruiting?

answers.label: More than half the day is admin
About 40 to 50 percent is admin
Around 30 percent is admin
Around 20 percent is admin
Under 15 percent, recruiters mostly recruit

questions.text: How clearly are roles split between recruiting, sales, admin, and operations?

answers.label: Everyone does everything, no clear lanes
Loose split, recruiters still do admin and sales
Defined roles, but lots of overlap
Clear lanes with occasional crossover
Sharp role separation with dedicated ops support

questions.text: How well do your tools talk to each other?

answers.label: They do not, we copy and paste between systems
One or two integrations, the rest is manual
Most core tools are connected, with some gaps
Solid integrations across ATS, CRM, email, and calendar
Fully integrated stack with automated workflows tying it all together

questions.text: On average, how many active job orders can one recruiter handle effectively?

answers.label: 1 to 3, and they are still overwhelmed
4 to 6
7 to 10
More than 15 with quality maintained

low.headline: Your recruiters are buried in work that should not be theirs
low.text: If recruiters are spending half their day on admin, you are paying recruiter salaries for assistant work. Every hour you free up here goes directly into more conversations, more submissions, and more placements.
steps: Track recruiter time for one week and identify the top 3 admin tasks eating their day
Move at least one of those tasks to an ops person or automation this month
Establish a minimum daily call and submission target so the time you free up actually converts

mid.headline: Your team is productive, but capped by tooling
mid.text: Your recruiters are doing real recruiting work, but they are losing time at the seams between tools. Closing those seams is where the next 20 percent of capacity lives.
steps: Map your tool stack and identify every manual handoff between systems
Automate the top 3 handoffs using a workflow tool like n8n
Rebalance recruiter loads so the highest performers get the most active orders

high.headline: Your team is humming, now expand the ceiling
high.text: You have clean role lanes, integrated tools, and recruiters who actually recruit. The next move is raising the ceiling on what one recruiter can handle by giving them AI-assisted support.
steps: Deploy AI assistants for first-touch outreach, screening, and scheduling
Add real-time dashboards so recruiters self-manage workload
Pilot a model where one senior recruiter runs 20 plus orders with junior or AI support

questions.text: How do you track core KPIs like submissions, interviews, and placements?

answers.label: We do not track them consistently
Manual spreadsheets updated weekly
Reports pulled from the ATS on request
Standing weekly dashboard reviewed by the team
Live dashboards with alerts on key thresholds

questions.text: How much do you trust the numbers coming out of your systems?

answers.label: Not at all, the data is a mess
A little, we always double check
Mostly, with known exceptions
Strongly, the data is clean
Completely, audited and reconciled regularly

questions.text: How fast can you answer a question like which client is most profitable this quarter?

answers.label: Days of digging
A few hours of pulling reports
An hour or so in the ATS
A few minutes in a dashboard
Instant, the dashboard answers it on demand

questions.text: How well can you forecast next quarter's revenue from current pipeline?

answers.label: We guess based on gut feel
Rough estimate from open orders
Manual forecast updated monthly
Pipeline-weighted forecast updated weekly
Live forecast with confidence intervals tied to historical conversion rates

low.headline: You are running the firm on instinct, and it is expensive
low.text: Without trustworthy data, every decision takes longer and costs more. You cannot fix bottlenecks you cannot see, and you cannot bet on what is working if you do not know what is working. Reporting is not a nice-to-have, it is how you stop guessing.
steps: Pick 5 core KPIs and commit to tracking them weekly, even manually at first
Audit your ATS data and clean up the fields that feed those 5 KPIs
Build one simple dashboard, even a spreadsheet, that you review every Monday

mid.headline: You have data, but it is not driving decisions fast enough
mid.text: You can pull numbers when you need them, but the lag between question and answer is too long. By the time you spot a problem, it has been costing you for a week or more. The fix is moving from pull reporting to push dashboards.
steps: Build live dashboards that surface your top KPIs without anyone having to pull a report
Add alerts on key thresholds so problems surface before the weekly review
Standardize a weekly numbers meeting that is data-first and gut-feel-second

high.headline: Your data is sharp, now use it to compound
high.text: You trust your numbers, you can answer questions fast, and your forecasts hold up. The next layer is predictive, using the data you have to drive the decisions you have not made yet.
steps: Build predictive models for placement likelihood by client and role type
Use historical data to optimize recruiter assignment automatically
Productize your reporting and offer client-facing analytics as a premium service

cta.headline: Ready to turn your score into more placements?
cta.description: You know where the bottleneck is. Now let's build the system that fixes it. Book a 30-minute strategy call and I'll walk you through exactly what to automate first, what to leave alone, and what one change will surface the most placement capacity for your firm.
